rationale: Evidence: iteration 4 (sensor x widened to -0.03..0.03, otherwise iteration 1's controller) scored 57.85, below iteration 1 at 75.97. Progress fell on the s-bend (0.29 to 0.157) and oval (0.16 to 0.153). Line losses did drop (s-bend 1.95 to 1.0, slalom 2.0 to 1.0) and s-bend oscillation fell (0.23 to 0.14), but max_error stayed at 0.062 to 0.064 on every track. The wider spread costs signal on the bends, and the score is driven mainly by progress. The Evaluator's requested change applies: progress fell below iteration 1 levels, so I revert the sensor x positions to -0.02..0.02 and test a larger footprint instead. Change: sensor_size 0.012 to 0.016, with the iteration 1 spacing and controller (kp 2.0, kd 0.2, base_speed 1.4, ki 0, last_direction, weights -2..2) unchanged. Expected result: a larger footprint reads the tape earlier and more continuously at the same spacing, so line_loss_events should fall without giving up the s-bend progress of about 0.29. I expect max_error to stay near 0.06 to 0.065 since the geometry reach is the same. Hypotheses: (H1) the larger footprint reduces line losses while keeping progress at iteration 1 levels; (H2) if progress drops, the footprint is not the limit and the next lever is kd near 0.15 for the s-bend oscillation of 0.23. Measurements wanted: progress per track (s-bend and oval against 0.29 and 0.16), line_loss_events on s-bend and slalom, max_error and its location, steering_oscillation, and completion_time if any run finishes.
